app.name: Homebody
app.tagline: Home workout planner and load calculator

common.comingSoon: This screen is on its way.

chest.name: chest
chest.about: The pectoralis major. Brings the arms together in front of the body: presses, push-ups, flyes.

shoulders.name: shoulders
shoulders.about: The deltoids: front, middle and rear heads. Overhead presses, lateral raises and bent-over raises.

traps.name: traps
traps.about: Upper back and neck. Lift and squeeze the shoulder blades: shrugs, upright rows.

neck.name: neck
neck.about: The neck muscles hold the head and protect the cervical spine. Train them smoothly, without jerking.

biceps.name: biceps
biceps.about: The two-headed muscle of the upper arm. Bends the elbow: curls, chin-ups.

triceps.name: triceps
triceps.about: The three-headed muscle of the upper arm, about two thirds of its size. Straightens the elbow: close-grip presses, dips, skull crushers.

forearms.name: forearms
forearms.about: The forearm muscles are responsible for grip. They work in almost every pull and in wrist exercises.

abs.name: abs
abs.about: The rectus abdominis and the obliques. They flex and rotate the torso and keep it rigid in a plank.

lats.name: lats
lats.about: The widest muscles of the back, the ones that create a V shape. Pull the arms down and towards the body: pull-ups, rows.

middle_back.name: middle back
middle_back.about: The rhomboids and the middle traps. Squeeze the shoulder blades together: bent-over rows, reverse flyes.

lower_back.name: lower back
lower_back.about: The spinal erectors. Keep the spine straight in deadlifts, good mornings and back extensions.

glutes.name: glutes
glutes.about: The gluteus maximus, the strongest muscle in the body. Extends the hip: bridges, squats, lunges.

abductors.name: abductors
abductors.about: The gluteus medius and the hip abductors. Stabilize the pelvis and knees and move the leg out to the side.

adductors.name: adductors
adductors.about: The inner thigh. Bring the legs together and assist in squats and lunges.

quads.name: quads
quads.about: The front of the thigh. Straightens the knee: squats, lunges, step-ups.

hamstrings.name: hamstrings
hamstrings.about: The back of the thigh. Bends the knee and extends the hip: Romanian deadlifts, bridges.

calves.name: calves
calves.about: The gastrocnemius and the soleus. Calf raises, jumps, walking.

notes.lightestTooHeavy: Even the lightest weight is on the heavy side: do fewer reps and build up gradually.
notes.notEnoughWeight: Not enough weight for the target rep range: slow the lowering phase down to 3 seconds.
notes.bigStep: A big weight jump: fewer reps than usual for now, they will come back next week.
notes.tooManyReps: That is a lot of reps: switch to a harder variation or slow down, 3 seconds on the way down.

shell.notSaved: Storage is unavailable: changes will be lost when you close the page.
shell.saveFailed: The last change could not be saved.

loadError.title: Your saved data could not be read
loadError.body: Nothing was changed or deleted. You can start over with a clean profile, which erases the data saved on this device.

settings.intro: Any change rebuilds the plan immediately. Your weight edits and exercise swaps are kept.

scale.title: Overall load
scale.about: Raises or lowers the working weights of every exercise in one move. The calculator picks new weights from your equipment and recalculates the reps. Exercises where you entered the weight or reps yourself follow your numbers and do not change.
scale.label: Weights relative to the calculation

equipment.title: Equipment at home
equipment.about: The plan is rebuilt right away: exercises that need missing equipment are replaced with ones you can do, and the weights are recalculated.
equipment.listHint: Separate the weights with spaces or commas, for example 2.5, 5, 7.5. The calculator only picks weights from this list.
equipment.unchanged: The exercises in the plan did not change.
equipment.unchangedAdded: The exercises in the plan did not change: what is already there fits better, but new options are available for swapping and in the library.

settings.about: Exercises, photos and instructions come from the open Free Exercise DB (Unlicense). The calculation uses the Epley formula for the estimated one-rep max, prescribes effort as reps in reserve (RIR) and progresses weekly according to your training level. Homebody is not medical advice.

sample.title: This is a sample plan.
sample.body: Body weight 80 kg, dumbbells up to 24 kg, three 45-minute sessions a week. Enter your own details and the plan will be recalculated.

plan.empty: Pick at least one training day in the settings to build a plan.

blockDone.title: Block complete
blockDone.body: Every session is ticked off. Press “Start the next block” at the bottom of the page: the new plan continues from the weights you reached.

nextBlock.title: Next block
nextBlock.pending: Press the button when you finish this block.
nextBlock.body: A new plan for {{weeks}} will start on the first Monday after {{date}} and continue from the weights you reached, including your edits. The overall load returns to 100%, counted from the new weights.

volume.title: Weekly volume
volume.about: Working sets per muscle; secondary work counts as half a set. The marked zone is {{min}}–{{max}} sets, the optimal range for the “{{goal}}” goal.
